clinical_knowledge.topic: Full-thickness supraspinatus rotator cuff tear with subacromial impingement evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Full-thickness supraspinatus rotator cuff tear with subacromial impingement is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Discuss conservative vs surgical management options, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: right shoulder weakness, pain when lifting arm above head, and night pain waking him up

Key HPI features: 54M carpenter reports 6-month worsening right shoulder pain located over the lateral deltoid area. Pain is triggered by overhead activities and reaching behind his back. Complains of sharp catching sensation when lowering the arm from abduction and severe night pain when lying on the right shoulder.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 74, BP 132/82. Inspection reveals mild right supraspinatus fossa muscle wasting compared to left. Active abduction limited to 100 degrees with pain arc between 60-120 degrees. Neer and Hawkins-Kennedy impingement signs strongly positive. Positive drop-arm test and Jobe (empty can) test demonstrating weakness in supraspinatus testing. Right shoulder MRI shows full-thickness tear of the supraspinatus tendon (1.8 cm retraction) with subacromial bursitis.
Relevant background/PMH: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Hyperlipidemia
Current medications: Metformin 1000mg BID, Atorvastatin 20mg daily
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Full-thickness supraspinatus rotator cuff tear with subacromial impingement.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Subacromial bursitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Night pain.
management_principles: Discuss conservative vs surgical management options

Given functional demands of carpentry work and full-thickness symptomatic tear, refer to orthopedic sports medicine/shoulder specialist for arthroscopic rotator cuff repair and subacromial decompression
Initiate pre-op physical therapy for range of motion and scapular stabilization
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

history.answer: My right shoulder has been aching terribly, and I can barely lift my arm above my head.
The pain is only in my right shoulder, right over the outside of the muscle. My left shoulder feels completely fine.
It started gradually about six months ago and has been steadily getting worse.
It is a constant dull ache, but it turns into a sharp pain whenever I raise or lower my arm. At its worst, it gets up to a six or seven out of ten.
No, I haven't seen any swelling, redness, or heat over the joint.
I don't have morning stiffness that lasts, though the shoulder feels stiff and sore if I rolled onto it in my sleep.
Raising my arm overhead, reaching behind my back, and lying on my right side make it much worse. Resting my arm down at my side gives me some relief.
It wakes me up multiple times every night, especially whenever I roll over onto my right shoulder. It has been ruining my sleep.
My arm feels weak and gives out when I try to lift things overhead. I can hardly hold my tools up anymore.
Yes, I feel a sharp catching and clicking sensation whenever I bring my arm back down from the side.
I can walk fine, but I can't lift heavy lumber or hold power tools overhead at all. As an independent carpenter, I am terrified of losing my livelihood.
There was no sudden fall or accident. It just crept up slowly after decades of heavy overhead carpentry work.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or sweating.
I used to get occasional muscle soreness after heavy workdays, but I have never experienced persistent weakness or pain like this before.
No, I have not had any unusual fatigue, low-grade fevers, or weight loss.
No skin rashes, mouth ulcers, hair thinning, red eyes, or dry mouth at all.
No lower back stiffness in the morning, heel pain, or swollen sausage fingers.
No diarrhea, pain when urinating, discharge, or sore throat recently.
I rarely drink, haven't eaten excessive meat or seafood, and don't take water pills.
I have never had steroid injections in my shoulder, taken steroids by mouth, or had any joint surgery.
I have been in a faithful monogamous relationship with my wife for over twenty years, with no other partners.
No, my neck feels fine, and there is no numbness, tingling, or shooting sensation going down my arm.
I think I tore one of my rotator cuff tendons from decades of heavy overhead work.
I would like to get an MRI to confirm what is going on and find out whether physical therapy or surgery is best for me.
I have had type 2 diabetes and high cholesterol for a few years, both controlled with daily tablets.
I have never had surgery and have never stayed in a hospital.
I take metformin 1000 milligrams twice a day and atorvastatin 20 milligrams once a day. I tried over-the-counter Tylenol, but it barely helps.
I have no known allergies to any medicines.
I have never smoked in my life.
I only have a beer on rare special occasions, maybe once a month.
I am a self-employed carpenter, right-hand dominant, and I live with my wife.
My father had high blood pressure, but there is no history of rheumatoid arthritis or other joint conditions in my family.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 132/82 mmHg, heart rate 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.8 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.

Inspection reveals mild right supraspinatus fossa muscle wasting compared to the left without erythema or warmth; palpation elicits tenderness over the right lateral deltoid and subacromial space; active abduction is limited to 100 degrees with a painful arc between 60 and 120 degrees; passive range of motion is preserved; and Neer, Hawkins-Kennedy, drop-arm, and Jobe empty-can tests are all positive on the right.
Right shoulder abduction and supraspinatus strength are reduced to 4/5 with pain, whereas bilateral elbow, wrist, and hand strength are fully intact at 5/5.
Sensation to light touch and pinprick is intact and symmetric across all upper extremity dermatomes, including the right axillary nerve distribution.
Biceps, brachioradialis, and triceps deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally with no abnormal reflexes.
Cervical spine active range of motion is full without paraspinal tenderness, and Spurling maneuver is negative bilaterally.
Skin inspection shows no rashes, psoriatic plaques, tophi, or nail pitting on either hand or arm.
